questions.question: Why do softmax([1,2]) and softmax([101,102]) return the same weights?
options: Softmax rounds all scores to zero before normalizing
The lists have the same number of elements, so scores are ignored
Subtracting the maximum makes softmax invariant to adding a constant
Softmax returns the raw input whenever it sees two values
questions.explanation: The implementation subtracts max(scores), leaving the same difference of one in both lists.

questions.question: What does dot_attention return besides the weighted context vector?
options: A single class label for the whole source sentence
The unnormalized dot-product matrix for every decoder layer
Only the index of the largest encoder state
One normalized attention weight for each encoder state
questions.explanation: It softmaxes one score per encoder state and returns the context together with the complete weight list.

questions.question: What error does dot_attention raise when an encoder state has a different length from the decoder state?
options: ValueError describing the length mismatch
IndexError after silently padding the shorter vector
No error; zip truncates the longer vector
A zero context with no diagnostic
questions.explanation: The explicit validation checks every encoder state before calculating dot products and raises ValueError on mismatch.

questions.question: In additive_attention, what does v_a do after the tanh projection?
options: It expands every encoder state back to the vocabulary size
It turns each attention-dimension vector into one scalar score by a dot product
It supplies the final weighted context without softmax
It chooses which source tokens to delete
questions.explanation: The code computes dot(v_a, combined) for each encoder state, producing the score that softmax will normalize.

questions.question: What is the shape relationship in matvec(M, v)?
options: M must be square and the result always has the same length as v
Only the first row is multiplied; all other rows are ignored
Every row of M must have len(v), and the result has one value per row
v is treated as a string of token IDs rather than numbers
questions.explanation: The helper validates each row length and computes one row-dot-vector value for every row of M.

questions.question: How do Luong dot attention and Bahdanau additive attention score a decoder/source pair here?
options: Both use only token frequency and never inspect hidden states
Dot attention concatenates strings, while additive attention sorts them
Additive attention removes the softmax step that dot attention requires
Dot attention uses a direct dot product; additive attention learns projections, tanh, and v_a
questions.explanation: dot_attention scores decoder_state against h directly, while additive_attention combines projected states before its scalar projection.
